confirmed.claim: The readback loop is `for (i, entry) in enumerate(x_entries)` with `_read(entry, ẋbuf_at(exec))` and a per-column `partials` loop over all columns
confirmed.evidence: src/linearize.jl:370-378: x entries are `(site, DerivRead)` pairs read as `_read(entry, seeded_exec)`; the partials split goes through `_readback!` (src/linearize.jl:564-571) once per group of `width` columns, inside the `Iterators.partition` loop. `ẋbuf_at` appears nowhere in src/.
confirmed.fix:
for (i, (_, entry)) in enumerate(x_entries)         # rows of A and B
    ẋ₀[i] = _readback!(A, B, i, _read(entry, seeded_exec), group, n_x)
end
for (i, entry) in enumerate(y_entries)              # rows of C and D
    y₀[i] = Float64(_readback!(C, D, i, _read(entry, seeded_exec), group, n_x))
end
confirmed.note: `_readback!` writes the group's partials into the `x` matrix for columns up to n_x and into the `u` matrix after. The snippet's two column ranges are right in effect.

ver.evidence: src/linearize.jl:357-369 loops `for group in Iterators.partition(1:N, width)`. It reads x rows with `for (i, (_, entry)) in enumerate(x_entries)` and `_readback!(A, B, i, _read(entry, seeded_exec), group, n_x)` (:363-364). The entry is the DerivRead half of an `(site, DerivRead)` pair, and `_read` takes the executor itself (src/readers.jl:590). `_readback!` (linearize.jl:578-586) fills only the group's columns. No `ẋbuf_at` exists in src/, and `git log -S'ẋbuf_at'` finds only c347a010, the walkthrough's own commit. The grouped loop has been there since the first code commit, 4f795b30, which predates the walkthrough's promotion. No record covers the full-column sketch.
ver.fix:
for group in Iterators.partition(1:N, width)        # one evaluation per group of `width` directions
    # seed the group's sites, then evaluate!(exec)
    for (i, (_, entry)) in enumerate(x_entries)      # rows of A and B; entry is the DerivRead
        ẋ₀[i] = _readback!(A, B, i, _read(entry, exec), group, n_x)
    end
    for (i, entry) in enumerate(y_entries)           # rows of C and D
        y₀[i] = Float64(_readback!(C, D, i, _read(entry, exec), group, n_x))
    end
end
# _readback! writes partial `pos` of the group's direction k into A/C (k ≤ n_x) or B/D (k > n_x)
ver.note: D-272 backs the code's grouping, which the walkthrough's own section 7 describes. No entry backs the doc's full-column loop. Writing the sketch with or without the `_readback!` helper are both faithful, so the fix is not unique.

confirmed.claim: Neither §14.8, the `trim!` docstring nor the `TrimProblem` docstring says that the guess is projected into the box before the search.
confirmed.evidence: src/trim.jl:667-674: `d0 = clamp.(guess, lower, upper)`, so a guess outside the bounds starts the backend at the bound while setup's condition and first evaluation (trim.jl:597-606) use the unclamped guess. Only the `solve` docstring (trim.jl:222-223) says "a `d0` that is not `NaN` already lies within the bounds". Spec 13851-13857 says only that bounds are honored by step projection.
confirmed.fix: Add to §14.8 "Box bounds" and the `trim!` docstring: "The service projects `guess` into the box once before it calls the backend, so a backend never sees a start outside the bounds."

ver.evidence: src/trim.jl:666-674 clamps the guess into the box once, `d0 = clamp.(...)`, before `solve`. The setup evaluation at trim.jl:597 still uses the unprojected guess. In the probe, guess u=10.0 in box [-1, 3] showed condition calls at 10.0, 10.0, then 3.0, and returned solution u=3.0, status=stalled, saturated=[(:u, :upper)]. §14.8 (13792-13802) says only that d0 is packed and that bounds are honored by step projection (D-070). The trim! docstring (trim.jl:500-557) and the TrimProblem docstring (trim.jl:24-66) are silent on it, and no log or pending text records it.
ver.fix: Add to §14.8's "Box bounds and saturated decisions": "The search starts from the guess projected into the box, so a guess outside it starts at the nearest point inside, and every point the backend sees and returns lies in the box. Setup's guess evaluation reads the guess as authored." Add to the `trim!` or `TrimProblem` docstring: "The search starts from the guess clamped into the bounds."

The callers pass `build.structure` (trim.jl:598, linearize.jl:316, model.jl:314, sim.jl:841). In the probe, `root_inputs = [:in, :e, :pu]` equals `input_faces(root) = ["in", "e", "pu"]`, and the shortfall was one UninitializedInputs naming [:e, :pu]. | The mechanism matches.
